messages:
Sam: Heads up — p99 for short-seq chat on pool-a jumped ~2.4x around 11:12 UTC, only on nodes in host group a-3.
Ingrid: same, started right after the overnight driver roll. KV cache hit rate collapsed (~18%) and kernel autoselect flipped to generic GEMM frequently.
Mike: attaching quick nsys notes — kernel_launch_latency jumped, and sm_efficiency dropped to ~40% during spikes. 
Mike: snippet: ```KernelLaunch        3.2ms -> 6.1ms, flashattn_v2 kernels rarely chosen, fallback_gemm dominates```
Ingrid: nsys also shows frequent GPU_PREEMPT events on those hosts, small context-switch stalls between kernels.
Rachael: could be noisy-tenant preemption from infra batch jobs? autoscaler logs show higher reclaim count for a-3.
infra-bot: [alert] host a-3 GPU_PREEMPT detected 2026-03-17T11:12:04Z (event_id=ev-190999).
Yash: interesting — driver 535.* was rolled last night to pool-a. pools on 534.x unaffected. Might be driver/firmware change causing kernel-selection heuristics to mis-evaluate workspace availability.
Sam: can we reproduce on a canary host? If driver is the trigger we should rollback on 1-2 hosts and run a shortseq workload.
Ingrid: repro steps I used: run short-seq synthetic (seq_len=64, batch=4, kv_cache warm) for 20m and watch autokernel decisions + KV hit rate. I saw autoselect switch to fallback within ~3m after a preempt.
Mike: uploaded nsys tar to s3://redwood-debug/1909998888/nsys.tgz and flamegraph summary to the thread.
Yash: quick mitigation: force kernel_hint=flashattn_v2 in the runtime routing for affected model group — reduces p99 by ~30% in my test, but increases memory pressure a bit. Good short-term test but not a permanent fix.
Sam: plan: 1) Schedule rollback to 534.67 on a single canary host in a-3. 2) Run Ingrid's repro harness and collect nsys/nvml. 3) If repro matches, open driver OEM ticket with attached traces.
Rachael: assigning eng-runtime oncall + infra to coordinate the rollback and canary run. @infra oncall please confirm window. :eyes:
Ingrid: also capturing KV cache alignment metrics and eviction counts; will paste the CSV shortly.
Sam: thanks — if rollback proves it, we do broader roll-back and then coordinate with drivers. If not, we'll hunt scheduler/autoscaler reclaim policy.
